rationale: Bacteroides vulgatus ferments glucose and lactate as primary carbon sources under anaerobiosis. Glucose uptake (15 mmol/gDW/h) is preferred; lactate (8) provides secondary fermentation. Arginine (3) supplies both carbon and nitrogen. Ammonium (2) covers direct N assimilation. Growth at 0.55 /h is limited by nitrogen availability (5 mmol in vs. 8 mmol needed per g biomass). Fermentation yields acetate, butyrate, propionate, CO₂, and H₂. Carbon balance: 38 mmol in = 22.6 (growth) + 15.4 (products). Confidence high; strategy aligns with known Bacteroides metabolism in anaerobic batch culture.
